status: Illustrative dimensionless engineering experiment; not fitted to human data
units: dimensionless linear response coefficients; rotation in radians per unit load

spatial_nonidentifiability.reason: P3(2y+1) is orthogonal on [-1,0] to polynomials of degree <=2. Rigid-body spring assembly contains only zeroth, first and second moments of side density. Three-point Gauss integrates degree <=5 exactly.
spatial_nonidentifiability.claim: Exact continuum alias within this reduced model, not an assertion that real PDL follows this density law

resting_pose_example.claim: Same incremental mobility can coexist with an imposed wrong resting pose. Unloading recovers that imposed pose; trauma, healing and drift were not simulated.

limits: Unit forces define linear response coefficients, not finite physical deformations or recommended human loads.
Rigid crown/root omits enamel, dentin and pulp deformation, restored thickness, crack propagation, contact area and fatigue.
Small-displacement static elasticity cannot predict healing, permanent repositioning, drift after support withdrawal, perfusion or physiological acceptance thresholds.
Very stiff illustrative support is not a diagnostic signature or a biological simulation of ankylosis.
